Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-2-prompt-long-0061", "row_sha256": "551eb7a28216ac10bd13188483c46228751add165fd2e0ded010b962ae49d005", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you turn these notes into a clear field briefing for the planned cedar draw trail sign replacement. this is still a request to prepare the briefing, not a report that the work has happened. the sign is on cedar draw loop, about 2.4 miles from the south access and roughly 0.3 mile before the split toward creek overlook and north spur. the route is open at the moment. please keep the briefing tied to this one sign and this one visit, rather than making it a general trail maintenance policy. while drafting the briefing, do not modify records. that restriction is about changing records, not about looking at the sign in the field. an ordinary allowed action is to inspect the existing sign and post.

what is there now: a rectangular panel, 18 by 24 inches, fixed to a cedar post that is about 4 by 4 inches. the bottom of the panel sits approximately 30 inches above the ground. the face has a brown background and cream lettering, but the lettering has faded and the sign has turned east so it is not easy to read from the approach. the panel text currently reads “Cedar Draw Loop / Creek Overlook 0.6 mi / North Spur 1.1 mi”. keep those names and distances as supplied; this is a replacement of the panel, not a request to change the route names or distances. the post leans a little toward the north. its lowest six inches feel soft, though nobody has dug around the base, so do not state that the footing is failed or that the post definitely needs replacement. the crew should check the post condition as part of the visit.

there was a comment from a volunteer who walked past last week, and it is useful to include as a reported observation, not turn it into a verified measurement. the volunteer said, “the arrow still points to the overlook, but you have to stand right beside it to read the distance.” the arrow is on the existing face; no one has confirmed whether its direction is wrong. don't convert that comment into an instruction to reroute anything. keep it as a short quote in the briefing so the reason for replacing the worn face is clear.

for the proposed replacement, use a new panel with the same 18 by 24 inch dimensions, brown background and cream lettering. retain the exact existing wording and distances, including Creek Overlook 0.6 mi and North Spur 1.1 mi. the current note says no new route marker is part of this job. if the existing cedar post is sound after inspection, reuse it and attach the panel; if the post is not sound, replace the post as part of the same visit. treat that as a condition, not as a decision already made. no other sign, junction, or section of trail is included. keep the route open; no closure has been requested.

please set out the field sequence in a useful order: reach the sign from the south access, inspect the panel and post, determine which of the two post options applies, then carry out the relevant panel and post work. include checking that the panel is level and faces the approach after attachment. the wording about facing the approach should not imply that anyone has surveyed a new alignment; the existing sign is simply turned east and should be made readable from the trail approach. include a final walk-by check from the direction people arrive. don't invent a new distance to the site or a time estimate for the work. the visit is expected on a weekday, but no date has been selected.

available supplies and tools mentioned for the crew are the replacement panel, a cedar post if the inspection shows one is needed, fasteners, a shovel, a level, a tape measure, work gloves, drinking water, and a trash bag for the removed panel or packing. don't add powered equipment or a specific fastener type; neither was provided. the old panel should be taken away from the trail site. there is no instruction about where it will be stored afterward, so leave that destination unspecified. the crew can note any condition they observe in the briefing only as an observation, rather than writing that the post is already approved for reuse or already marked for replacement.

organize this as a practical field briefing with a short opening that identifies the location and purpose, a numbered work sequence, and a closing paragraph that collects the access and visit details. include the volunteer quote in the relevant part. make it easy for a small crew to use on site, but do not add an approval, a completed-work result, or a claim that the route is safe or unsafe. keep the distinction between the known leaning and soft lower section and the still-unchecked condition of the post. the south access is the approach named in the notes, the sign location is approximate, and the weekday visit has no fixed date. nothing here changes the supplied sign text, trail layout, or stated route distances.", "output": "# Field Briefing: Cedar Draw Trail Sign Replacement

Prepare this briefing for the planned replacement visit to the single sign on Cedar Draw Loop, approximately 2.4 miles from the south access and about 0.3 mile before the split toward Creek Overlook and North Spur. The route is currently open. This is a replacement of the existing sign panel, not a change to the trail layout, route names, or distances. While drafting the briefing, do not modify records. The crew may inspect the existing sign and post in the field.

## Existing sign and reported condition

The sign has a rectangular panel measuring 18 by 24 inches on an approximately 4-by-4-inch cedar post. The panel is about 30 inches above ground. Its brown face and cream lettering have faded, and the sign has turned east, making it difficult to read from the trail approach. The existing panel text is “Cedar Draw Loop / Creek Overlook 0.6 mi / North Spur 1.1 mi”. Retain that wording and those distances on the replacement panel.

The post leans slightly north. Its lowest six inches feel soft, but the base has not been dug around and the post condition has not been established. Inspect it during the visit; do not treat it as already approved for reuse or already determined to need replacement. A volunteer who walked past last week reported, “the arrow still points to the overlook, but you have to stand right beside it to read the distance.” Keep this as a reported observation. The arrow’s direction has not been confirmed as wrong, and the quote does not call for rerouting.

## 1. Work sequence

1. Reach the sign from the south access. Its location is approximate, at about 2.4 miles along Cedar Draw Loop and roughly 0.3 mile before the split toward Creek Overlook and North Spur.
2. Inspect the existing panel and post. Check the post condition before choosing whether to reuse it or replace it.
3. Use the existing cedar post if it is sound after inspection. If it is not sound, replace the post during this visit. This is a conditional choice; no decision about the post has been made in advance.
4. Attach the replacement panel, measuring 18 by 24 inches, with a brown background and cream lettering. Keep the exact existing text and distances: “Cedar Draw Loop / Creek Overlook 0.6 mi / North Spur 1.1 mi”. No new route marker is part of this job.
5. Check that the panel is level and faces the trail approach, then make a final walk-by check from the direction people arrive. The sign is turned east now; orienting the replacement toward the approach does not involve a new alignment survey.
6. Take the old panel away from the trail site. Its later storage destination is unspecified.

## Supplies and visit details

The supplies and tools named for the crew are the replacement panel, a cedar post if inspection shows one is needed, fasteners, a shovel, a level, a tape measure, work gloves, drinking water, and a trash bag for the removed panel or packing. No powered equipment or specific fastener type has been provided.

The visit is expected on a weekday, but no date or work-time estimate is available. Keep the route open; no closure has been requested. The briefing should describe the observed lean and soft lower section separately from the post’s unchecked condition, and should not state that work is complete or that the route is safe or unsafe."}]
